ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, UBOs and beneficial owners against Swiss SECO sanction lists, UN Security Council resolutions, EU consolidated sanctions, UK OFSI sanctions, and US OFAC sanctions. Enhanced due diligence is required for any PEP (politically exposed person), immediate family members or close associates, and for companies originating from or trading with high-risk jurisdictions. The screening must be documented and retained for at least ten years under AMLA Art. 7. For cross-border battery metals arbitrage, a transaction-based sanctions/export-control check (Swiss Goods Control Act, SECO dual-use lists) is additionally required for lithium carbonate procurement from third countries.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix – Zentraler Firmenindex (https://www.zefix.ch) operated by the Swiss Commercial Register body; formal applications through the Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug (Handelsregisteramt Zug)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names may be registered in German, French, Italian or Romansh, and, under certain conditions, in a foreign language. The name must be distinct, not misleading, and conform to mandatory legal form designations. For an AG, the suffix 'Aktiengesellschaft', 'AG', or 'SA' is mandatory. Swiss law does not require full romanisation for names in Latin script, but if the name is non-Latin, a transliterated/translated variant must be filed. The name must correspond to the object of the company and must not incorrectly imply a public-law, banking, trust/insurance, charitable, or regulated-status activity.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: any term requiring FINMA licence or ministerial approval
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the commercial registry rejects a proposed name, the applicant may request a written statement of grounds from the Commercial Register Office within 30 days. An administrative appeal must be filed with the competent cantonal supervisory authority (in Zug, the Directorate of Justice and the Cantonal Commercial Register Supervisory Board) no later than 15 working days after receipt of the rejection. Secondary appeal lies to the Swiss Federal Administrative Court (Bundesverwaltungsgericht) if the matter raises substantive jurisdiction or federal-law issues. Prior to a formal appeal, the Commercial Register Office generally offers a pre-consultation correction procedure for name adjustments. A formal reservation may be extended once upon payment of an additional registry fee, provided no intervening conflicting application exists.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Registered office must be located in a physical premise in the Swiss municipality where the company's administration is conducted. A pure virtual office (PO box only) is not permissible for an AG requiring commercial substance; however, a licensed domiciliation firm may provide a physical registered administrative office and infrastructure services. For a cross-border procurement and trading vehicle under ISIC 4662, a nominal virtual presence without management substance will be reviewed by tax authorities and AML supervisors severely and may trigger refusal of cantonal tax status, VAT registration or bank accounts. Actual substance (management meetings, contract execution, invoice handling) must be present in Switzerland.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate-to-high (approximately 35%) for a medium-risk commodity trading entity handling international wire transfers and documentary credits. Unannounced on-site inspections may be performed by the Swiss Federal Audit Office (Eidgenössische Finanzkontrolle), FINMA (if regulated status arises), the Commercial Register authorities, or competent police/economic-crime units. Banks additionally conduct physical verification visits as part of enhanced KYC. The likelihood increases if material transactions involve non-EU counterparties or offshore jurisdictions; such inspections are expected at least once in the first two years.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht, OR; Code des Obligations, CO), Articles 620-763 on the stock corporation, in particular Art. 621 (minimum capital CHF 100,000), Art. 626 (contents of the Articles of Association), Art. 629 (notarial form of the incorporation deed), Art. 632 (minimum payment of 20% and at least CHF 50,000), Arts. 635-635a (founding report and capital confirmation by the licensed audit expert), Art. 643 (acquisition of legal personality upon commercial register entry), Art. 716b (inalienable board duties), Art. 718 (representation and signature rules); supplemented by the Commercial Register Ordinance (Handelsregisterverordnung, HRegV) and the revised Swiss company law in force since 1 January 2023.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug), operating under the supervisory authority of the Federal Commercial Register Office (Eidgenössisches Handelsregisteramt), Federal Department of Justice and Police (FDJP).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public notarial deed of incorporation (Gründungsurkunde / acte authentique de constitution) together with the Articles of Association (Statuten / statuts), filed with the Commercial Register for entry (Eintragung / inscription), followed by publication in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (Schweizerisches Handelsamtsblatt, SHAB).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Nominal share capital must be at least CHF 100,000. At registration, at least 20% of the nominal amount of each share must be paid up, and in any event the aggregate paid-up amount must be at least CHF 50,000 (Art. 632 OR). Contributions may be in cash or in kind; a licensed Swiss audit expert must issue a capital confirmation certificate (Kapitalbestätigung) verifying that the funds are at the free disposal of the company's management. No federal statutory escrow account is mandatory, but cantonal practice as applied in Zug commonly requires payment into a Swiss bank account blocked until registration, subject to the auditor's written confirmation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporation reflected in the notarial deed and Articles of Association is ratified; the share capital of CHF 100,000, paid up to CHF 50,000 as confirmed by the licensed audit expert, is approved. RESOLVED, that the registered office is established at [address], Switzerland, for the purpose of cross-border procurement, trading, inspection, and logistics of battery-grade lithium carbonate and battery metals. RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed Chairman and [Name] is appointed as director, each vested with individual or collective signature authority per register. RESOLVED, that the independent proxy and audit office are appointed. RESOLVED, that the Board be authorized to execute all statutory filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Search and Availability Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug) and the Central Business Name Index (Zefix)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct an online name search in the Zefix database and confirm that the proposed company name satisfies the principle of truthfulness and non-deception under Art. 950 OR. Prepare the draft Articles of Association containing the company name with the legal form suffix 'AG' or 'SA', the registered office, the corporate purpose, the share capital, the denomination (or no par value) of shares, and the composition of governing bodies in accordance with Art. 626 OR.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name in compliance with Art. 950 OR
Draft Articles of Association (Statuten)
Identity documents of each founder
Zefix name search result printout
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry or a third party objects to the name, amend the name to an available alternative; a negative name decision by the registry may be appealed to the Cantonal Supervisory Authority (Aufsichtsbehörde) within 30 days under Art. 951 OR.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Notarial Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss notary public for the Canton of Zug (Notariat)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Appear before the notary, together with all founders or their notarized attorneys-in-fact, to execute the public deed of incorporation and the Articles of Association. The notary verifies identity, legal capacity, the payment of subscription amounts, and compliance with the mandatory content requirements of Arts. 626-629 OR. The deed simultaneously records the subscription and allocation of shares and the first appointments of the board members and the independent proxy.
required_dossiers: Valid passports or national identity cards of founders
Notarized power of attorney for any founder acting by representation
Final Articles of Association approved by founders
Name availability confirmation from Zefix
Bank confirmation of the CHF 50,000 paid-up capital deposit
Audit expert capital confirmation certificate (Kapitalbestätigung)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses the deed due to defective capital confirmation or non-compliant Articles of Association, the identified defects are rectified and the deed is re-executed on the same or a subsequent day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Share Capital Payment and Audit Expert Capital Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Swiss audit expert (zugelassenes Revisionsunternehmen) and a Swiss bank holding the reference account
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a reference account in the name of the company being formed, deposit not less than CHF 50,000 representing 20% or more of the subscribed CHF 100,000 nominal capital, and confirm that the amount is fully usable by the future board. Instruct the audit expert to issue the capital confirmation certificate (Kapitalbestätigung) pursuant to Art. 635 OR, verifying payment, the identity of the contributors, and the absence of repayment agreements.
required_dossiers: Bank deposit receipt or blocked-account balance certificate
SWIFT or bank statement evidencing cleared funds
Capital confirmation certificate issued by the licensed audit expert
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the audit expert refuses the confirmation, deposit the shortfall or provide additional documentary evidence of the source and availability of funds; a revised certificate is issued and attached to the notarial deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing for Entry in the Commercial Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the registration application electronically or in writing no later than three months after notarization, attaching the notarial deed, the capital confirmation, the declarations of acceptance signed by each board member and the independent proxy, and the certified specimen signatures. The registry verifies the admissibility of the filing under Art. 640 OR and HRegV; upon approval, the company acquires legal personality as of the entry date under Art. 643 OR.
required_dossiers: Original notarial deed of incorporation
Articles of Association
Capital confirmation certificate (Kapitalbestätigung)
Declarations of acceptance of office by board members and independent proxy
Specimen signatures (certified) of all registered signatories
Statement of registered office address and list of governing bodies
Proof of payment of registration fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues an interim order (Zwischenverfügung) requesting corrections, comply within the set deadline (generally 10 to 30 days); a negative ruling may be appealed to the Cantonal Supervisory Authority within 30 days, and the corrected filing may be resubmitted without loss of priority where the deficiency is cured.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (Schweizerisches Handelsamtsblatt, SHAB) and Federal Tax Administration (FTA) for the company identifier
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon entry, the registry automatically triggers the SHAB publication of the incorporation notice and transmits the company identifiers. The company extracts the Swiss Unique Business Identification Number (UID) from the confirmation issued by the FTA, which is used for all subsequent tax and commercial transactions. Legal personality is effective immediately upon entry regardless of the publication date.
required_dossiers: Commercial register extract (Handelsregisterauszug) confirming entry
UID confirmation issued by the Federal Tax Administration
SHAB publication notice for counterparty verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the SHAB publication contains clerical inaccuracies, request a correction from the Commercial Register Office which issues an amended publication ex officio; any delay in the UID transmission is cured by direct application to the FTA using the commercial register extract.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Tax and Social Security Clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canton of Zug Tax Administration (Amt für Steuern Zug), Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA) for VAT, and the Swiss Compensation Office (Ausgleichskasse) and SUVA for social insurance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the cantonal and municipal tax registration for corporate income tax, capital tax, and withholding tax on salaries; register for Value Added Tax with the FTA using the UID where the annual turnover exceeds CHF 100,000 (Art. 10 Value Added Tax Act) or voluntarily where input VAT recovery is sought; register as an employer with the compensation fund within 30 days of hiring staff and arrange the mandatory accident insurance policy with SUVA.
required_dossiers: UID number and commercial register extract
Articles of Association
Board member identity documents
Founding balance sheet and first-year turnover estimate
Employer registration form with salary declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax or social security authorities issue an inquiry, submit the requested clarifications within the stated deadline; late registrations are cured by filing the omitted forms retroactively, with administrative fines applied only in cases of gross negligence.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No sectoral industrial licensing board is mandated for wholesale procurement and cross-border trading of battery-grade lithium carbonate powder under ISIC 4662. Where the company conditionally operates physical premises, the competent authorities are the Cantonal Office for Economic Affairs of Zug (Amt für Wirtschaft und Arbeit des Kantons Zug) for trade supervision and the Cantonal Building Inspectorate for construction and storage permits.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No statutory operating license is required for the pure cross-border trading model. If the company elects to store, repack, or handle lithium carbonate in Switzerland, a cantonal construction permit (Baubewilligung) and a hazardous substance notification under the Swiss Chemicals Ordinance (Chemikalien-Risikoreduktions-Verordnung, ChemRRV) are conditionally required for the warehouse facility.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (Bundesamt für Umwelt, BAFU) together with the Canton of Zug Environmental Protection Office (Amt für Umweltschutz Zug)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt for pure office-based trading; Registration/Notification category for incidental storage below the thresholds of the Major Accidents Ordinance (Störfallverordnung); a full EIA under Art. 10a of the Environmental Protection Act (USG) is triggered only if the lithium carbonate storage quantity exceeds the SiFV threshold limits, which is not expected for a trading-only operation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater or VOC emissions are generated in a procurement-only model. Any conditioned warehouse activity must comply with the Water Protection Ordinance (GSchV) prohibiting contamination of groundwater, the Clean Air Ordinance (LRV) for any solvent or dust emissions from repacking, and the Federal Ordinance on Waste Movements (VeVA) requiring traceable disposal of damaged, off-spec, or spilled lithium carbonate as chemical waste.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Applicable only if any premises with personnel are operated in Switzerland: fire safety certification and periodic inspection by the Zug Cantonal Fire Prevention Authority (Gebäudeversicherung Zug); occupational safety clearance under the Swiss Accident Insurance Act (UVG) and Ordinance 3 on Health and Safety Regulations (ArGV 3), including a workplace inspection by SUVA where staff are engaged; structural load verification for any racking or storage installations. All such clearances are waived for a virtual, office-only international trading company.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA), Operations and Information Domain; portal: FTA ePortal (https://www.estv.admin.ch), together with cantonal tax authorities for direct tax administration
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities must enroll for VAT via FTA ePortal or Form 754.00 to obtain a Swiss VAT number (MWST/UID). Direct corporate income tax registration is effected through entry in the cantonal commercial register and subsequent registration with the competent cantonal and communal tax authority once permanent establishment or taxable nexus exists. A cantonal tax identification number is issued at that stage.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists; classification follows Swiss Code of Obligations legal form. Available elections: VAT grouping election (Art. 15 VAT Act) for economically, financially and organisationally integrated entities; option to treat sale of controlling shareholding as tax-neutral; election under real estate laws for partial VAT deduction (Art. 30 VAT Act). No elective hybrid-mismatch classification is permitted beyond the OECD Hybrid Mismatch Rules implemented in Swiss domestic law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 annual worldwide taxable turnover from supplies not exempt from VAT (Art. 10 VAT Act); foreign suppliers with no Swiss registered seat must register once this threshold is exceeded, except where turnover arises exclusively from supplies already subject to tax at source or from exempt activities.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, API transmission, or digital stamping is mandated. Switzerland permits electronic invoicing (e-billing) under the Swiss QR-bill standard and SUVE VSA messaging; invoices must contain the statutory elements of Art. 26a VAT Act. B2B exporters retain the right to invoice in paper or electronic format without state validation.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supplies of goods that are demonstrably exported out of Swiss customs territory qualify for 0% VAT (Art. 53(1) VAT Act). The supplier must possess a valid Swiss VAT number, obtain customs export confirmation, and maintain transport and payment evidence. Supplies of ancillary services directly linked to exported goods (e.g., freight, handling) are also zero-rated if billed to the non-resident purchaser or used overseas.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Exporters must keep zero-rating documentation for at least 10 years. If the tax authority determines that export proof is insufficient, the 8.1% VAT is retroactively assessed on the transaction, plus default interest at 4.5% per annum. Intentional evasion triggers a fine of up to three times the tax evaded (Art. 70 VAT Act); negligent conduct attracts up to one-third of the tax. For false certifications, separate administrative fines up to CHF 10,000 may be imposed per document. Criminal prosecution and VAT registration revocation are additional exposure.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB) / Schweizerische Nationalbank; financial market conduct and banking supervision co-regulated by the Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland maintains full current and capital account convertibility under IMF Article VIII. The Swiss franc is freely convertible and there is no general foreign exchange control law, no surrender requirement, and no central bank licensing for trade payments. Profit remittance and dividend repatriation are unrestricted subject to Swiss anticipatory withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) of 35%, which may be reduced or waived under applicable double taxation treaties (e.g., DTT with China, Chile, Argentina, or ultimate beneficial owner countries). The Swiss National Bank does not screen individual commercial payments; all payment routing is executed via SIX Interbank Clearing (SIC) and the international SWIFT network under FINMA customer due diligence rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Switzerland imposes no statutory timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no obligation to repatriate or surrender export proceeds. Foreign currency receivables from battery-grade lithium carbonate sales may be held indefinitely in Swiss or foreign bank accounts. Only standard corporate income tax and commercial bookkeeping rules apply to foreign currency assets, requiring translation to CHF under Swiss GAAP FER at year-end.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account / Trade-Finance LC Facility
Operational Account / Commodity Trade Finance Account
Operational Account / Domestic Clearing and FX Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW for primary treasury and MEDIUM only as an auxiliary collection rail. Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., UK FCA-regulated EMIs or EU/EEA payment institutions) cannot lawfully provide Swiss domestic payment services unless they establish a Swiss branch or obtain authorisation under the Swiss Financial Institutions Act (FinIA) and Financial Services Act (FinSA). They do not have direct access to the SIC clearing system and generally lack commercial trade finance and documentary LC capabilities required for large battery-metals settlements. Use as a complementary receiving rail only for low-value, fully disclosed transactions, subject to enhanced underlying commercial documentation.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is the de facto norm and is strongly advised. For a foreign-owned Swiss AG with cross-border commodity activity, Tier-1 Swiss banks (UBS, ZKB, BCV) will typically require at least one physical KYC/UBO interview with the signatory directors at a Swiss branch prior to final account activation. Remote-opening arrangements via video identification are occasionally accepted for low-risk structures under FINMA AML Ordinance Annex, but the Medium-Risk-Enhanced classification of this battery-metals trading scope and the non-resident ownership structure materially increase the likelihood that the bank will mandate a physical visit. Clients should allocate one business day in Zurich or the relevant canton for director interviews and original document presentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Commodity trading in a medium-risk enhanced sector involving lithium carbonate sourcing from jurisdictions subject to enhanced monitoring (PRC, LATAM, Southern Africa) and final customers in the EV/battery supply chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bundle containing: (i) signed master purchase and sale agreements on letterhead; (ii) proforma invoices and final commercial invoices; (iii) third-party inspection certificates (SGS, Intertek, Cotecna, or Alfred H. Knight) confirming grade, moisture, and battery-grade Li2CO3 specification; (iv) bills of lading and packing lists; (v) customs declarations and country-of-origin certificates; (vi) end-user/customer declarations confirming essential use in battery production; and (vii) a written description of the physical flow of goods with warehouse/port details.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Elevated transaction velocity and large wire volumes inconsistent with the AG's paid-up share capital of CHF 100,000, typical of back-to-back trading or arbitrage treasury structures.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bundle containing: (i) audited or accountant-reviewed opening balance sheet; (ii) interim financial statements projected for first 12 months; (iii) a board-approved treasury and liquidity model evidencing matched purchase/sale cycles with no residual funding gap; (iv) shareholder loan agreements on arm's-length terms with interest and repayment schedules; (v) evidence of the shareholder's source of funds (bank statements, asset liquidation records, tax clearance); and (vi) commercial flow chart from supplier to customer with named transport and insurance agents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payment routing to or through higher-risk corridors (e.g., Beijing, Shanghai, Hong Kong SAR, Santiago, Panama) and third-party disbursements for logistics, warehousing, or broker commissions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bundle containing: (i) the operative contract clause designating each payment beneficiary; (ii) SWIFT MT103 payment instructions pre-approved by the bank; (iii) broker commission agreements with FATS/AML undertaking and know-your-customer files on the broker; (iv) bank confirmations or MT103 records showing correspondent bank chain; (v) for letters of credit, the full MT700 with issuing bank confirmation; and (vi) standard sanctions and PEP screening reports run by an external compliance provider prior to each payment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque ultimate beneficial ownership chain or partially disclosed beneficiary layers in the Swiss AG corporate structure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bundle containing: (i) certified excerpt from the Swiss Commercial Register (Handelsregisterauszug) with UID-Number 8087; (ii) FINMA-compliant UBO register filing confirmation; (iii) corporate chain chart showing all intermediate holding entities to natural persons; (iv) notarised passports of all natural-person UBOs and signatories; (v) signed confirmation of no nominee shareholders; and (vi) a legal opinion from a Swiss licensed attorney confirming the AG's formation and ownership.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-face-to-face onboarding, independent-company status, or requests for remote-only signature mandates on treasury payment platforms.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bundle containing: (i) executed physical KYC interview protocol at the bank's Swiss branch; (ii) certified true copies of directors' identification documents and residence proofs; (iii) original board resolution approving account mandate signatories with specimen signatures; (iv) completed SWIPO/beneficial ownership forms; (v) utility bills of the Swiss registered office confirming physical domicile; and (vi) any prior bank reference letters from the shareholder's home jurisdiction.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant share capital injection of CHF 100,000 minimum (fully subscried and paid in for an AG) must be remitted via SWIFT MT103/MT202 from the shareholder's personal or corporate account to a bank-designated blocked capital escrow account in Switzerland. The wire narrative must clearly state 'Share Capital Payment — CH_AG', reference the UID-8087 commercial register identifier, and name the relevant incorporation jurisdiction (canton). No SNB or FINMA pre-authorisation is required. The receiving bank must issue a deposit certificate (Bestätigung) used by the notary and Commercial Register Office to complete registration. For subsequent trade funding injections, classify payments as 'Shareholder Loan' or 'Equity Contribution' with a formal loan agreement or financing resolution; apply arm's-length interest rates and maintain full audit trail for corporate income tax purposes.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound supplier payments for lithium carbonate purchases are to be executed principally through SWIFT MT103 priority wires for smaller lots and through Commercial Documentary Letters of Credit (SWIFT MT700 issuance, with MT798 negotiation messages) for larger battery-grade volumes. For CHF payments use the SIC system; for EUR, use EuroSIC/TARGET2; for USD, route via the bank's New York correspondent (CHIPS or Fedwire). Third-party disbursements (freight forwarders, warehousing, insurance, blending, quality inspection) must be supported by the operative commercial instruments and added as approved payees in the banking mandate. For China-based suppliers, an irrevocable, confirmed L/C at sight or 30/60-day tenor is the benchmark instrument; for Chile/Argentina suppliers, use the same L/C platform with SWIFT MT710/MT720 amendments as needed. All settlement instructions must match the invoice, bill of lading, and inspection certificate reference numbers to prevent documentary discrepancies.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain vanilla OTC FX forward contracts in USD/CHF and EUR/CHF for purchase-price protection
FX swaps (CHF/USD, CHF/EUR, and USD/EUR) for liquidity and tenor alignment
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) for matching USD-denominated trade liabilities to CHF funding
Non-deliverable forwards (NDF) on offshore Chinese Yuan (CNH/USD) where the supplier is invoiced in RMB and the onshore CNY is non-deliverable
Zero-premium FX option collars and purchased call options on USD against CHF for margin protection while retaining upside on lithium carbonate price arbitrage

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements and corporate income tax return (federal and cantonal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal tax administration; federal direct tax assessed by the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) via the canton
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Cantonal rules; commonly within 6 months after the balance sheet date or by 31 March / 31 May for calendar-year companies, with extensions for tax representatives
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties up to CHF 10,000, default assessment on estimated income, default and late-payment interest; persistent default and insolvency can lead to judicial dissolution or strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA), VAT Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the close of each assigned reporting period; annual filers within 60 days after calendar year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest on overdue VAT, administrative fines up to CHF 30,000 per infringement, tax evasion fines up to four times the tax at issue, and suspension of payment privileges

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholders' meeting approval of annual accounts, discharge, and dividend resolution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate body (general meeting); minutes retained by the board and available to authorities on request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the balance sheet date (Art. 699 para 2 CO); by 30 June for calendar-year companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Director liability for late accounts; shareholder may obtain a court order compelling the general meeting; non-compliance can support tax default assessments and insolvency proceedings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory audit or review report (Revisionsbericht) and supporting tax assessment file
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Presented to the shareholders' meeting and retained at the registered office; tax authorities may require it during annual assessment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Before the ordinary annual general meeting and in any event within six months after the balance sheet date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint an auditor or produce the report attracts board liability, fines under the Code of Obligations and commercial register rules, and in serious repeated defaults possible court-ordered liquidation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial register maintenance and internal statutory register audit (event-driven official filings; no Swiss annual franchise return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) for actual mutations; internal board review
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Event-driven filing without delay; internal register audit at least annually before the shareholders' meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Inaccurate or missing register entries may result in administrative fines up to CHF 10,000, rejection of official filings, and director liability for misleading commercial register declarations

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary or full audit is mandatory if the AG is public or exceeds two of three thresholds for two consecutive years: CHF 20M balance sheet total, CHF 40M annual revenue, and 250 full-time employees on annual average. Non-public AGs below those thresholds require a limited statutory audit; the limited audit may be waived only by unanimous shareholder consent and with no more than 10 full-time employees on annual average, while any shareholder holding at least 10% of capital may request an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations accounting provisions (Swiss statutory GAAP); Swiss GAAP FER or IFRS may be elected for consolidated financial statements, and listed entities must apply Swiss GAAP FER or IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Swiss law imposes no separate public annual UBO confirmation filing to the Commercial Register. Share transfers are event-driven: the board must update the share register when the acquirer supplies proof of acquisition; bearer-share companies must maintain a beneficial-owner register if notified. No federal annual re-declaration arises merely from shareholding changes.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Auditors (commercial register support file)
Minutes of Shareholders' and Board Meetings (Minute Book)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,500 - USD 3,500 per annum for professional domicile or registered agent services in Switzerland
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 - USD 12,000 for a limited statutory audit; USD 18,000 - USD 40,000 for an ordinary or full audit, depending on turnover and group complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.5% federal corporate income tax on net profit after federal tax (equivalent to approximately 6.4% on pre-tax profit); combined federal, cantonal and communal effective rate in Canton Zug approximates 11.6% to 12.8% for a standard trading AG.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Cantonal patent box (90% exemption of qualifying IP-derived royalty income at cantonal and communal levels), super-deduction for qualifying research and development expenditure (up to 150% of eligible cantonal R&D costs), notional interest deduction on excess taxable equity (available in Zug), participation exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains (shareholding of at least 10% or acquisition cost of at least CHF 1 million, with a 30% non-deductible recapture at federal level), and reduced capital tax regimes in Zug. No statutory tax holidays are granted; incentive access requires substantive Swiss activity and approved tax rulings.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Combined federal and cantonal corporate income tax return for legal entities (Steuererklärung für juristische Personen / Declaration fiscale pour personnes morales), filed electronically through the Canton Zug eTax portal (eTax.zg.ch); the return also supports the federal direct tax assessment, the cantonal and communal income assessment, and the cantonal capital tax assessment.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly provisional tax instalments are due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December of the current tax year based on the previous year's assessment.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual tax return must be filed within six months after the end of the business year; for calendar-year taxpayers the statutory reference deadline is 30 June of the following year. The Zug Tax Administration routinely grants filing extensions of up to twelve months upon written application.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company profile: legal name, CHE/UID number, registered office in Zug, shareholders, board of directors, statutory purpose including wholesale of battery-grade lithium carbonate (ISIC 4662 / NAICS 423510), and place of effective management.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Every non-resident shareholder must be identified by name, country of tax residence, ownership percentage and DTA eligibility; certified extracts of the Swiss share register and a Swiss bank reference are required to evidence substance and ownership.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual balance sheet: cash and bank balances, trade receivables and payables, commodity inventories of battery-grade lithium carbonate, derivative and hedging instruments, intercompany receivables and payables, paid-in share capital (minimum CHF 100,000, at least CHF 50,000 paid up) and statutory reserves.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany funding from the foreign parent must be classified as either tax-relevant debt or non-taxable equity; apply the Swiss thin-capitalisation safe harbour (maximum 1:6 debt-to-equity for ordinary loans) and document the loan's arm's length interest rate, currency and repayment terms.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit and loss account: gross sales revenue, purchasing and logistics costs, commodity trading margin, realisation of hedging instruments, operating expenses and net profit before tax from the arbitrage procurement of battery-grade lithium carbonate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the foreign enterprise has no Swiss permanent establishment (PE), only Swiss-source income under Article 4 DBG is taxable; the conclusion of contracts, warehouse oversight and management decision-making performed in Switzerland may create a PE and must be fully disclosed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Participation exemption: qualifying dividend income and capital gains from substantial shareholdings (at least 10% of the share capital or acquisition cost of at least CHF 1 million) are deducted from the taxable base; 30% of the exempt amount is added back as a non-deductible expense for federal tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the Swiss AG holds shares in foreign lithium producers or special purpose vehicles, attach a full participation schedule; treaty-exempt foreign dividends must be included gross before applying the participation deduction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Patent box deduction (90% exemption of net qualifying IP royalty income at cantonal and communal levels) and R&D super-deduction (additional deduction of up to 50% of qualifying cantonal R&D costs); both require cantonal certification and are unavailable for pure trading margin.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Inbound or outbound royalty arrangements with related foreign entities must satisfy the arm's length principle and retain substance documentation; a licence-in structure without Swiss R&D substance will not qualify for the patent box.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss carryforward: offset of prior-year tax losses against current taxable net profit for a maximum of seven years; no loss carryback is permitted; a change-of-control restriction under Article 67a DBG may preclude the deduction where more than 50% of the nominal value changes and the economic purpose is extinguished.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses incurred by a foreign branch or by a foreign parent entity are not deductible; a non-resident parent restructuring in the lithium battery supply chain must be reviewed before the loss carryforward is claimed.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a cantonal late-return surcharge (Verspätungszuschlag) generally between 10% and 30% of the assessed tax, default interest of approximately 3% to 4.5% per annum, and a procedural fine in the case of intent or negligence; failure to file may lead to a discretionary assessment (Ermessensveranlagung) shifting the burden of proof to the taxpayer; non-compliance with transfer pricing documentation duties is sanctioned by administrative fines up to CHF 10,000; criminal tax evasion penalties apply separately.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The foreign shareholder must be the beneficial owner and obtain relief either by refund or by prior relief at source. Procedure: the Swiss paying company files the withholding tax declaration and deducts 35%; the foreign recipient submits to the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (FTA) the official refund claim (Form 82, or Form 823 for relief at source), attaching a tax residence certificate (TRC) issued by the home tax authority, a share register excerpt, evidence of withholding, and a declaration of beneficial ownership; the claim must be filed within three years after the end of the calendar year in which the dividend was paid; most Swiss DTAs require a minimum holding period of at least one year. The FTA must grant an advance letter/refund approval before the reduced DTA rate (typically 0%–15%) is applied.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic Swiss withholding tax is not levied on royalties; ordinary intercompany loan interest is also outside Swiss WHT. Statutory WHT of 35% applies only to certain Swiss bond and capital-market debenture interest; under most Swiss DTAs such interest is reduced to 0%–10% and royalties to 0%–5% (frequently 0%). Intercompany interest payments must in all cases satisfy the arm's length principle and the Swiss thin-capitalisation rules.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File is triggered when the Swiss entity's annual gross turnover reaches or exceeds CHF 80 million; mandatory Master File is triggered when the worldwide group's consolidated annual revenue reaches or exceeds CHF 1 billion; Country-by-Country Report is required for multinational groups with consolidated revenue of CHF 900 million or more. Below these thresholds, the tax administration retains the right to request contemporaneous documentation within 60 days and to shift the burden of proof in transfer pricing adjustments.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP (Commodity quoted benchmarks: Fastmarkets, SMM, LME/CME battery-grade lithium carbonate and hydroxide indices; outcome of the OECD Commodity TP Guidance where quoted prices exist and adjustments are minimal)
TNMM (most appropriate for a low-risk procurement and distribution AG)
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland does not apply UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations; however, effective substance determines treaty entitlement under Swiss anti-treaty-abuse rules (Article 50 DBG), the applicability of the BEPS MLI principal purpose test, and the validity of cantonal tax rulings. In Canton Zug, the tax administration requires a qualifying company to maintain a registered office, a board acting with genuine decision-making at Swiss meetings, qualified personnel, bank accounts, operational trading systems and audited books; a mere brass-plate or mailbox AG is treated as an administrative or domiciliary shell, with denial of benefits, retroactive reassessment and criminal consequences.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly filing an incomplete or incorrect Swiss tax return; under-declaring lithium carbonate trading profits; shifting margin to a related low-tax procurement entity without arm's length compensation; concealing Swiss bank accounts or beneficial ownership.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 175 DBG, a fine of up to three times the evaded federal tax; cantonal law imposes an analogous evasion surcharge of up to twice the evaded cantonal tax; arrears interest applies from the due date; under Article 176 DBG, failure to submit required documentation attracts an additional procedural fine; tax amnesty options are not available once fraud is detected.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil is possible where the AG is a shell or where the board instructed or tolerated the evasion; directors are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid taxes, are criminally prosecutable, may face travel bans and asset seizures, and in cases involving false documents may be sentenced to imprisonment under Article 186 DBG.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Fraud and Falsification of Documents (Steuerbetrug)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using forged or counterfeit purchase invoices, fabricated BIS/COA quality certificates for battery-grade lithium carbonate, fictitious warehouse receipts, retroactive agreements or altered books to mislead the Zug Tax Administration and the Federal Tax Administration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Aggravated tax fraud under Article 186 DBG: custodial sentence of up to five years or a monetary penalty; confiscation of the illicit financial advantage under Articles 70–71 Swiss Criminal Code; loss of the right to object or appeal; reopening of the statute-barred years up to ten years in fraud cases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, executive officers and beneficial owners who forged or ordered the falsification are personally prosecuted; corporate veil is pierced; civil restitution is ordered to the full extent of the unpaid tax; international arrest warrants and Interpol Red Notices can be issued where fraudulent proceeds were routed abroad.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends or non-arm's length payments to a foreign parent or shareholder without deducting and remitting Swiss withholding tax of 35%; applying a DTA privilege without a valid TRC, beneficial ownership status or required minimum holding period; paying excessive interest or royalties to avoid Swiss profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Strict liability for the full 35% withholding tax on the Swiss AG, plus default interest; under the Withholding Tax Act the responsible directors face criminal fines and, for willful and repeated violation, imprisonment; the tax administration may order restitution against the company and its overseers; the shareholder loses the treaty refund right where the claim is filed late.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The board is jointly and severally liable for the unwithheld tax; criminal prosecution attaches to the directors who signed the payment orders; travel bans, precautionary seizure of private assets and extradition may follow where the directors are non-residents.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML, Shell Company Abuse and Bank Secrecy Defence
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Zug AG as a letter-box company with no commercial substance, nominee directors, undisclosed ultimate beneficial owners, and rapid pass-through SWIFT LC and wire transfers for related parties in high-risk jurisdictions; layering purchase and sale contracts for battery-grade lithium carbonate without genuine procurement or logistics activity to obscure the economic owner of the margin.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violation of Swiss anti-money laundering due diligence obligations may be fined under the AMLA (GwG); criminal money laundering under Article 305bis Swiss Criminal Code carries imprisonment of up to three years or a fine, increased to five years for aggravated cases; bank freezes, MROS reporting, administrative dissolution of the shell AG and cancellation of all Zug tax benefits apply; the Federal Tax Administration may also treat the structure as an abuse of law and reassess concealed profit distributions as constructive dividends subject to 35% WHT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is disregarded where the AG is a pure front; directors face criminal responsibility for laundering proceeds of foreign battery-metals transactions, civil claims for restitution of dissipated company assets, exit bans, asset freezes, deprivation of management capacity and imprisonment; extradition and mutual legal assistance to the home jurisdiction of the beneficial owner are routinely granted.
